clue.text: Fighting with knights' page, as bad dream fades at last

indicators.note: bad here means spoilt or out of order, so the letters of dream are jumbled
at last points to the final letter of the word fades

explanation.surface: A young page dreams of jousting, the nightmare fading at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' turns DREAM into DARME; 'at last' takes S from fades.
explanation.definitionFit: A pas d'armes was a medieval chivalric combat, a joust held by knights defending a passage.

clue.text: Proclaim on eradicating even this disorder

indicators.note: removing the even-numbered letters leaves only the odd ones of the run Proclaim on

explanation.surface: Someone announces a campaign to wipe out this illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eradicating even' keeps letters 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9 of 'Proclaim on'; the surface's eradicating fits the polio vaccination campaigns.
explanation.definitionFit: Polio is a viral illness of the nervous system, a disorder that can cause paralysis.

clue.text: Fish for small kipper?

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a kipper is read as one who kips, that is takes a nap, so a napper

explanation.surface: Seems to ask for a fish suitable for a small smoked herring.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipper looks like a smoked fish but is read as one who kips (sleeps).
explanation.definitionFit: Snappers are a family of tropical sea fish, such as the red snapper eaten widely.

clue.text: Team loses a point, falling short at Wembley, perhaps

indicators.note: falling short means the word is cut off before its last letter
loses means the team gives up a letter taken out of its name

parts.note: Arsenal is a London football team
S is south, one of the compass points

explanation.surface: A football team drops points and comes up short at the national stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal is a north London football club. 'loses' takes S out of ARSENAL to give ARENAL; 'falling short' drops its final L.
explanation.definitionFit: Wembley Stadium in London is an example of a sporting venue, a large stadium used for matches.

clue.text: The fish that got away, you say? It's a mix-up

indicators.note: you say signals that the phrase is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a fish that escapes is a catch, or take, that the angler missed

explanation.surface: An angler's tale of the one that got away is dismissed as confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken quickly, 'missed take' (a lost catch) sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A mix-up is an error or confusion, a blunder of exactly that sort.

clue.text: Boatman & crew: visionaries covering a great distance

indicators.note: covering means the outer word wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: seers are prophets who see visions of the future
far means a great distance away

explanation.surface: The setter and his crew are dreamers who travel a long way.
explanation.walkthrough: Boatman is the setter's pseudonym, which makes the sailors' definition apt.
explanation.definitionFit: A boatman and his crew are sailors, people who travel by sea.

clue.text: See 9
More than one heavyweight is alone, pulled up after initial concussion

indicators.note: initial picks the first letter of the word concussion
pulled up in a down clue means the words are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: solo means alone, unaccompanied

explanation.surface: A boxer, isolated, is lifted off the canvas after a concussion.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'pulled up' reads the words from the bottom upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Colossi is the plural of colossus, a giant statue or a person of great size and importance.

clue.text: Part of old civilisation moving into Chile

indicators.note: moving suggests the letters shift into a new order

explanation.surface: A piece of an ancient culture is relocated to South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges the letters of 'into Chile'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Neolithic, or New Stone Age, was an early period in human history when farming began.

clue.text: Fish beat up a lobster

indicators.note: beat up suggests the letters are battered into a new shape

explanation.surface: Some fish assault a lobster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat up' rearranges the letters of 'a lobster'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloaters are whole herrings lightly salted and smoked, so they count as fish.

clue.text: Cold salmon prepared at home: commonplace now

indicators.note: prepared means made up or arranged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Cold salmon has been made ready in the kitchen, nothing special these days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges the letters of 'Cold salmon'.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for modern conveniences: the household amenities such as central heating that are standard in homes today.

clue.text: Excitement from the person that announced defrosted fish

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so we want a word sounding like it

parts.note: who is the relative pronoun meaning the person that

indicators.note: defrosted means with the ice taken away

parts.note: plaice is a flatfish

explanation.surface: Fuss over someone who declared their fish had thawed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'announced' turns WHO into HOO; 'defrosted' removes ICE from PLAICE, leaving PLA.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoopla is noisy fuss and commotion, a fair synonym for excitement.

clue.text: First mate's boat in legend was used to get wife

definitions.text: First mate's boat in legend was used to get wife

parts.note: Adam was the first man and the first husband, so the first mate's is Adam's
a RIB is a rigid inflatable boat

explanation.surface: A first mate's boat featured in a legend about winning a bride.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also tells the Genesis story: Eve, Adam's wife, was made from his rib.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, God formed the first woman from a bone taken from Adam's side, giving him a wife.

clue.text: Some fish in need of bigger boats?

definitions.text: Some fish in need of bigger boats?

parts.words: Some fish in need of bigger boats?
parts.note: a nod to the film Jaws, where the line 'you're gonna need a bigger boat' is spoken on seeing the great white

explanation.surface: Seems to wonder which fish need larger vessels.
explanation.walkthrough: In Jaws, the hunters see the huge predator and say they need a bigger boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Great whites and their kin are large predatory fish that make anglers want sturdier craft.

clue.text: Very sad indication for our planet

parts.note: split the entry into two words: the first, made sore, would rearrange into the name of our world

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a sign pointing to the Earth.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as HEART SORE, the entry reads as an anagram instruction: HEART, made 'sore', gives EARTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone heartsore is grieving deeply, with an aching heart, so profoundly unhappy.

clue.text: Head of state crazy to execute guerrilla leader, one of 101?

indicators.note: to joins the crazy head of state to the next pair, which comes after them
Head of picks the opening letter of the word state

parts.note: potty is British slang for mad
to execute a task is to do it

indicators.note: leader points to the opening letter of the word guerrilla

explanation.surface: A mad head of state is set to execute a rebel chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 101 refers to The Hundred and One Dalmatians, a story full of spotted dogs. POTTY is British slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dalmatian is a dog with spots, and the book features a hundred and one of them.

clue.text: Vision of Boatman: a plot, they say

indicators.note: they say means the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: the setter Boatman is I, so of Boatman is I's, and a plot of land is a site

explanation.surface: The setter's dream turns out to be a scheme, according to rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, I'S SITE (the setter's plot of land) sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Vision is the faculty of seeing, the same as sight through the eyes.

clue.text: An apostle in Rome alone, cut by a spear, even

indicators.note: cut by means the word alone is split open with the other letters placed inside

parts.note: solo means alone, by oneself
taken as written

indicators.note: even picks the even-numbered letters of the word spear

explanation.surface: An apostle in Rome, isolated, is pierced by a spear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'even' takes letters 2 and 4 of spear. The grid's SAO mixes in the Portuguese form; the Italian name for the saint is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Paul the Apostle is called by his Italian name in Rome, where he was martyred.

clue.text: Fish shortage following cutback

indicators.note: following means this piece comes after the other one

parts.note: lop means to prune, and written right to left it gives these letters; the clue joins the two words into one
a lack is a shortage

explanation.surface: A shortage of fish after reductions in quotas.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'cutback' as two words: cut (LOP) turned back gives POL.
explanation.definitionFit: Pollack is a food fish of the cod family found in North Atlantic waters.

clue.text: Goldfish with starter of dory and crab perhaps found here

parts.note: OR is gold in heraldry, and char is a fish of the trout family
OR is gold in heraldry, and char is a fish of the trout family

indicators.note: starter of picks the first letter of dory

explanation.surface: A recipe of goldfish with dory and crab as a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goldfish' gives two pieces: OR (heraldic gold) and CHAR (a fish). The crab is the crab apple, not the shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: Crab apples are fruit trees, the kind grown in an apple orchard.

clue.text: Smell fish on seafront

indicators.note: on means the fish is placed after, resting on, the other piece

parts.note: the front of sea is its first letter
tench is a freshwater fish of the carp family

explanation.surface: Detecting a fishy odour by the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places TENCH after the front of 'sea'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stench is a strong, foul odour, a bad smell.

clue.text: Teams rely (after losing wingers) on a smaller number, their leader going down

indicators.note: on means the first piece is followed by the second
losing wingers strips the outer letters of rely, leaving its middle
the first letter of the number drops to the bottom, which in a down answer is the end

parts.note: seven is a number below eleven

explanation.surface: Football teams that lose their wingers depend on fewer players, captain included.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'going down' sends the first letter to the bottom, the end of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Football and cricket sides field eleven players, so a team is called an eleven.

clue.text: Sporting fish roe from theoretical hybrid

indicators.note: a hybrid is a cross, so the letters are mixed into a new form

explanation.surface: Fish eggs from some sporty crossbreed of theory.
explanation.walkthrough: Take ROE out of the letters of THEORETICAL and rearrange the rest ('hybrid').
explanation.definitionFit: Athletic describes a person or event connected with sport and physical fitness.

clue.text: Bigger fish eaten by little fish with no resistance

indicators.note: eaten by means swallowed inside the other word

parts.note: fry are newly hatched young fish
an eel is bigger than fry

explanation.surface: A predator is swallowed by tiny fish that put up no struggle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With no resistance' looks like wordplay removing R; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To act freely is to act without obstruction or anything holding you back.

clue.text: Japanese fish: ultimate in "sole" music

parts.note: fugu is the Japanese pufferfish, eaten as a risky delicacy

indicators.note: ultimate in picks the last letter of sole

explanation.surface: A Japanese fish served with a touch of sole, set to music.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotes round 'sole' hint at soul music, but sole simply supplies its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A fugue is a contrapuntal composition, a form of classical music built on a repeated theme.

clue.text: Looks suggestively at au pair's bottom in the grounds

indicators.note: in means the letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: lees are the dregs or grounds that settle at the bottom of wine or coffee

indicators.note: bottom picks the last letter of pair

explanation.surface: Someone ogles a nanny's behind in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Grounds looks like gardens but means dregs, LEES; 'bottom' takes the last letter of 'pair'.
explanation.definitionFit: To leer is to look at someone in a lewd or knowing way.

clue.text: Raw cod, flounders and yellow fish

indicators.note: flounders means struggles clumsily, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A fish counter of raw cod, flounder and some yellow fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Flounders looks like a third fish; it is the anagram verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is slang for cowardly, and a fish can mean a person, so a yellow fish is a craven type.

clue.text: Fish definitely returning to land in the Irish Sea

parts.note: to angle is to fish with rod and line

indicators.note: returning means the word is turned back to front

parts.note: yes is a definite affirmative

explanation.surface: Fishing trips that surely come back to an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses YES to SEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglesey is the island off the north-west coast of Wales, set in that sea.

clue.text: Report to reveal one may be in the soup

definitions.text: one may be in the soup

indicators.note: report means the sound of a word, as a gun's report is its bang

parts.note: to leak information is to reveal it secretly

explanation.surface: A news story threatens to expose someone who is in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the soup' sounds like being in trouble; here it is literal, as in leek and potato soup.
explanation.definitionFit: The leek is a vegetable of the onion family, often cooked in soups such as cock-a-leekie.

clue.text: Fishy substitute for universal part of theories of Flora, Fauna etc

indicators.note: substitute for means one piece replaces another in the word

parts.note: guesses are theories or conjectures
U is the British film certificate for universal
fishy means suspicious or odd

explanation.surface: Odd replacement for a universal element in theories of plants and animals.
explanation.walkthrough: Flora and Fauna look like plants and animals but are Roman deities. U is the universal film rating.
explanation.definitionFit: Flora was the Roman deity of flowers and Fauna a Roman fertility deity, both female divinities.
